scope: Proposition 5.7 (The regularity interface for the coupled system) of the manuscript “The nonmaximal anti-de Sitter Penrose Inequality and original-data rigidity” (preprints/The-nonmaximal-anti-de-Sitter-Penrose-Inequality-and-original-data-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9e2b9ba2768918dc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 60. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider a family of smooth solutions (f, Z) on smooth finite domains with uniformly controlled interior and boundary patches. Assume |f| + |Df| + |Z| ≤ M and the following structural bounds, uniformly in the family: (i) The f-equation has the form of Equation (5.1), with b ≥ c0 > 0 and bounded G. Its actual matrix and source are smooth functions of (x, Z, f, Df) on the bounded variable range, including at Df = 0. The value of f on each boundary face is constant. (ii) After multiplication by the coordinate volume density, the Z-equation is ∂i aij (x, Z, f, Df)∂jZ + Bi (x, Z, f, Df)  = Q, |Q| ≤ C(1 + |DZ|2 + |D2 f|2 ), (5.26) where a is symmetric and uniformly elliptic and B is bounded. The functions a, B and Q, as a function also of (DZ, D2f), are smooth on the ranges on which they are used. (iii) Each boundary component for Z has either constant Dirichlet data, or bounded total conormal flux. In the latter case its equation can also be solved as ∂νZ = H(x, Z, f, Df), (5.27) where H is smooth on the bounded variable range. These faces are disjoint and have no edges where the type of data changes. Assume that the derivatives of the displayed smooth functions and the geometry are bounded to the order needed for each stated estimate. Then f and Z have uniform local classical estimates of every such finite order, including at the boundary. The constants are independent of the size of a finite exhaustion domain if the patch geometry and all the displayed data bounds are independent of that size.
